summary: Multi-agent orchestration layer wrapping Claude Code and Codex CLIs. Features swarm topologies (mesh, hierarchical, ring, star), 100+ specialized agents, persistent HNSW vector memory, 314 MCP tools, and agent federation. 66k+ stars as of July 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — shares the CLI-subprocess approach but targets swarm/parallel execution rather than deterministic state machines. The HNSW episodic memory pattern could inform HID-188 (cross-run memory), but the overall architecture is very different from AgentForge's sequential pipeline.

summary: Production-ready merger of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel for .NET and Python. Ships sequential, concurrent, handoff, group-chat, and Magentic-One orchestration patterns; graph-based workflow engine; checkpointing and pause/resume; human-in-the-loop approvals. Orchestration layer reached 1.0 in July 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the graph workflow engine with checkpointing maps to AgentForge's partial-retry gap (HID-186), but that issue already exists. Magentic-One pattern (manager+specialists with goal-directed dispatch) is conceptually adjacent to HID-72 (auto-dispatch loop). No new capabilities not already tracked.

summary: LangGraph shipped node-level caching, dynamic tool calling, type-safe streaming (version v2 format), and CLI deployment commands in 2026. Core at 1.2.1 as of May 2026. LangChain 1.0 deprecated AgentExecutor in favor of LangGraph runtime.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses, not LangGraph's graph runtime. Node-level caching and dynamic tool routing don't apply. AgentForge already has SSE streaming (runEventEmitter.ts). No verifiable gap opened.

source: Google Research: centralized vs parallel agent error scaling (Jan 2026)
summary: Google evaluated 180 agent configurations: centralized coordination contained error amplification to 4.4x while independent parallel agents amplified errors 17.2x. Validates sequential/centralized orchestration for reliability.
relevanceToAgentForge: High (validation) — confirms AgentForge's sequential pipeline design choice. Not an actionable gap but good evidence to cite when defending the sequential model against pressure to add parallelism (which was already rejected as speculative execution).

summary: CrewAI open-source 1.15.18 released August 27 2026. Crew Studio adds prompt-assisted flow construction, single-agent/crew/router nodes, 1000+ connectors, reusable agents, source export, testing, tracing, and deployment in one workspace.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — CrewAI's Crew Studio is a visual builder for multi-agent flows; AgentForge uses a deterministic state machine driven by Linear issues. No direct mapping to an open gap.

summary: 2026 practitioner consensus: tiered memory (context window as RAM, core editable memory, searchable recall, archival vector/graph store). Key new emphasis: write-path policy (what to persist) matters more than retrieval. MemRL: episodic memories as learned retrieval policy. Letta's model cited as reference implementation.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the write-path policy insight is interesting for HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory). Letta's tiered model could inform implementation design. However HID-188 already tracks this; no new issue needed.

summary: Karpathy ran 8 agents (4 Claude + 4 Codex, each with own GPU) to run ML pretraining experiments on his nanochat codebase. Experiment reportedly revealed current agent capability limits. Also coined 'agentic engineering' as successor to vibe coding (Feb 2026).
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — experiment was about ML research automation, not orchestration tooling. 'Agentic engineering as oversight' framing aligns with AgentForge's human-in-the-loop design but does not surface a new gap.

summary: Active community fork of AutoGen by its original creators after Microsoft moved AutoGen to maintenance mode in Oct 2025. Apache 2.0 licensed. Continues active feature development on the multi-agent conversation framework.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AG2 is a Python multi-agent conversation framework; AgentForge is a TypeScript/Fastify orchestrator using CLI subprocesses. No direct integration path.

summary: New 2026 TypeScript repo (~21.7k stars) positioning itself as an open-source managed agents platform for turning coding agents into teammates that take assigned tasks and track progress. Tagged agent-orchestration.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — concept of 'agent as teammate' with task tracking is very close to AgentForge's own model (Linear issues + orchestrated agent execution). Worth monitoring to see if their task assignment patterns offer any novel techniques, but no specific verifiable gap identified yet.
